PullRequest.Title: chat: fix flaky collapse-anchoring completion tests
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes the flaky `ChatListWidget › persistent progress collapse anchoring › completion during collapse preserves reading position (…)` tests. They failed in main CI [489793](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=489793) (Linux Electron unit) and in PR CI on Oct 23 ([job 120344241857](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39941097839/job/120344241857)) and Oct 25, on unrelated branches. Different `canceled` and `incremental` variants failed, and each time only this changed:

```
-  "runningTransition": false
+  "runningTransition": true
```

## Why

After the response streams more content and the thinking preview starts collapsing, the test waited a **real** `timeout(40)` and then required `getAnimations()` to still contain a running transition. The collapse transition (`grid-template-rows`) lasts **180 ms**. On a loaded agent, the 40 ms timer can fire after the transition has finished. A finished CSS transition is no longer returned by `getAnimations()`, so `runningTransition` is `false`. That also means the response no longer completes mid-collapse, which is the scenario under test. The anchoring and padding assertions still passed in every hit.

The product side doesn't depend on wall-clock timing. `ChatListWidget` follows the collapse through `transitionrun`/`transitionend` events and resize observations.

## Fix (test only)

Right after `refresh()` starts the collapse, the test pauses the transitions and seeks them to 40 ms, then lets two frames run so the widget sees the partially collapsed layout. Then it completes or cancels the response, resumes the transitions, and waits for them to finish as before. The response therefore always completes 40 ms into the collapse, however slowly the agent runs. `runningTransition` now checks that the collapse is mid-way (`currentTime < duration`).

## Validation (headless Chromium, `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --run …/chatListWidget.test.ts`)

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original, with the 40 ms timer firing late (temporarily `timeout(200)`) | **8/8 variants fail**, `runningTransition: false` (the CI diff) |
| Fixed, ×20 | 20/20 (8 variants each) |
| Fixed, all cores busy with CPU burners, ×10 | 10/10 |
| Mutation: `preserveScrollPosition` made a no-op | 8/8 fail on `scrollTop` / `paragraphStayedAnchored`, so the test still guards anchoring |
| Whole file, ×3 | 119 passing each time |

eslint is clean, and tsc shows no errors in the file.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Headless browser test: response completion or cancellation 40 ms into a thinking-preview collapse across canceled, incremental-rendering, and auto-scroll-hold variants
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test creates and lays out the chat widget, starts the CSS collapse, pauses and seeks the bounded descendant animation set, waits for two requestAnimationFrame callbacks so layout observes the intermediate state, completes or cancels the response, resumes animations concurrently, then waits for animation completion and stable layout. All changed work is on the test's critical path and no product runtime path is changed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser animation-frame scheduling, CSS animation control, and layout/compositor advancement
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getAnimations query, two serial requestAnimationFrame callbacks, and one concurrent wait over the bounded animations beneath one preview per test variant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: After starting the same 180 ms transition, the test waited on a 40 ms timer and then awaited the transition's remaining duration; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The two frames and resumed transition must finish before assertions. Seeking to 40 ms leaves roughly the same remaining transition work as the prior real 40 ms timeout, while making the intermediate state deterministic.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eight fixed test variants (2 canceled states × 2 incremental-rendering states × 2 hold states); within each test, work scales with the small set of animations under one thinking preview rather than chat history or user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each test performs its two frame waits serially. Descendant animations are paused/resumed in bounded synchronous loops and their completion promises are awaited concurrently with Promise.all; the suite's variants are defined as separate tests and do not create a changed aggregate concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache, cache key, miss path, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior is involved. Each isolated test constructs a fresh widget and animation state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed browser-frame and animation work from the diff and helper implementation. High confidence that it is test-only and bounded; no external expensive boundary is reached by the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: requestAnimationFrame delay varies under headless CI load, but the changed count is fixed at two frames and replaces a 40 ms wall-clock wait; there is no realistic unbounded multiplicity or product-facing latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The changed work is bounded to eight test variants, replaces rather than adds to the prior mid-transition wait, resumes all captured animations before awaiting completion, and does not affect shipping product execution.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full one-file diff. Traced test multiplicity, animation ownership, frame scheduling, layout stabilization, external boundaries, cache behavior, and concurrency. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR is not a concrete shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame attribution.
